marks.gloss_en: דתנן: בית שמילאהו תבן או צרורות וביטלו -- מבוטל; ביטלו אין, לא ביטלו לא -- the Rabbis' side
straw he does not intend to clear, and plain earth: these are the dispute of R' Yosei and the Rabbis
ותני עלה, רבי יוסי אומר: תבן ואין עתיד לפנותו הרי הוא כעפר סתם ובטל -- R' Yosei's side
inferred from the mishna: nullified, yes; not nullified, no -- straw without explicit nullification is not nullified
אמר ליה רבא: הא דירה סרוחה היא, ואין אדם דר בדירה סרוחה
Rava: that is a sagging dwelling, and no one dwells in a sagging dwelling
even though he nullified them -- because his intent is void against that of all people
straw that he nullified: it is a diminution
above twenty amot with palm-leaf ends hanging within twenty: if their shade exceeds their sun, valid; if not, invalid
Abaye thought to say: ten tefachim high with leaf-ends hanging within ten -- if their sun exceeds their shade, valid
above twenty amot, with a platform built along the whole middle wall holding the sukkah minimum: valid
a platform at the side: four amot from its edge to the wall -- invalid; less than four amot -- valid
the mishna (17a): a breached house roofed over the breach -- four amot of roof from the wall to the sekhakh invalidates; less, valid
taught: dofen akuma applies even where the wall is not itself fit to be a sukkah wall (being above twenty)
a platform in the middle: four amot from its edge to the wall on every side -- invalid; less -- valid
taught: dofen akuma applies on every side, not only on one
below ten tefachim, dug out to complete ten: three tefachim from the pit's edge to the wall -- invalid
